correctness.rationale: With 3 rows, n positive columns and n+2 links, sum_j(deg column_j -1)=2. Hence either one degree-3 column, with P<=n-1+5/2<2n-2 for n>=4, or two degree-2 columns. If their common rows number one, column contribution <=2(n-2) and row contribution <=2, with equality iff all singleton columns hit common row; if identical degree-2 column neighbors, third-row no-isolate forces at least one disjoint singleton column, so P<=2n-5. This proves unique maximizer, labeled 3n(n-1), and Ferrers P=n+1. Independently generated all no-isolate 3xn matrices with n+2 links at n=4,5,6 and computed exact rational overlap sums: 522,2595,11673 admissible and maxima P=6,8,10 with labeled optimum counts 36,60,90. The infinite n theorem follows from the exhaustive structural degree-excess argument.
